caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 743 of 2012
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Mahmuda Begum Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners 
Abdul Matin Khashru, Senior Advocate, instructed by Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondents
parties:
Md. Abdul Awal, former authorized officer-3 RAJUK ----- Petitioner
Vs.
SM Asaduzzaman and another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J.:- This criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 20.11.2011 passed by a division bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 13624 of 2007 making the Rule absolute. 

 3. On 28.10.2003, Md. Abdul Awal, authorized officer-3, RAJUK being informant lodged an first Information Report with the Mirpur Police Station. Dhaka under sections 420/406/467/ 468/471/34 of the Penal Code. His case is that accused, namely. (1) Dr. Sultan Ahmed (2) AKM Nurun Nabi, (3) Rabiul Hoque. (4) Nikil Chandra Das (Surveyor) and (5) SM Asaduzzaman (Authorized Officer-1) presently Executive Engineer (under suspension). RAJUK Rhaban, Dhaka, in collusion with each other created forged deeds and papers of ownership. Accused Nos. 1-3 without being the owners of CS Plot Nos. 730 and 731 (part) of Mouza-Senpara parbata under holding No. 150/1. P.S. Mirpur, Dhaka measuring and area of .52 acres of land created false and fraudulent documents and obtained clearance certificate of the land. Accused No. 4 went to survey the land and put signature on the clearance certificate accused No. 5 without accepting Tk. 60,000/- as fees illegally approved the plan by misusing power and accused Nos. 1-3 being fully aware that they are not the owner of the land constructed a 9 storied building on the said land and sold the apartments to the purchasers and as such, they committed criminal offence. 

 4. On the basis of the First Information Report, Mirpur Police Station Case No. 141 dated 28.10.2003 corresponding to G.R. No. 4481 of 2003 under sections 420/406/467/468/471/34 of the Penal Code was started. 

 5. During investigation of the case, the police found prima facie case and submitted charge sheet against three accused persons and proposed discharging petitioner respondent No. 1 and another by filing final report. After that the learned magistrate discharged them from the case but no naraji petition was filed and the informant being the petitioner filed a revisional application being Metro Criminal Revision No. 600 of 2006 before the learned Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge Dhaka under section 439 A of the code of Criminal Procedure. The application under section 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Second Court. Dhaka, who after hearing the parties by his judgment and order dated 08.05.2007 set aside the order dated 16.05.2006 passed by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka and directed the Magistrate to take next step in accordance with law. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 08.05.2007 passed by the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka, respondent No. 1 filed a Criminal Miscellaneous Case under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 13624 of 2007. 

 7. Learned Judges of the High Court Division, upon hearing the parties, made the Rule absolute and set aside the judgment and order dated 08.05.2007 passed by the learned Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge. Second Court, Dhaka in Metro Criminal Revision No. 600 of 2006 setting aside the order dated 16.05.2006 passed by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka in Mirpur P.S. Case No. 141(10)2003 corresponding to G.R. No. 4481 of 2003 and quashed the proceeding so far as it relates to respondent No. 1. 

 12. The High Court Division came to a finding that the investigating officer completed the entire investigation properly and that he obtained signature of respondent No. 1 and the signature of one Nikhil Chandra Das and found that there is no resemblance of the signature of respondent No. 1 with his signature contained in the approved plan and as such, the investigating officer proposed discharging the petitioner as there was no prima facie case or material available against him. 

 15. Admittedly, relying upon the report of the hand writing expert, the High Court Division quashed the proceeding So far as it relates to respondent No. 1. The opinion of hand writing expert does become evidence unless he deposes before the Court. Therefore, the High Court division was not justified in quashing the proceeding so far as it relates to respondent No. 1. The learned Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, however, on consideration of the materials on record set aside the order dated 16.05.2006 passed by the learned Metropolitan magistrate accepting the final report an discharging respondent No. 1 from the case so far as it relates to respondent No. 1. The judgment delivered by the learned Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge is based on proper appreciation of law and fact. On the other hand, the judgment of the High Court Division is not based on proper appreciation of law and fact and as such interference is called for by this Division. Accordingly, this civil petition for leave to appeal is disposed of and the impugned judgment passed by the High Court Division is set aside. 

 16. The learned Metropolitan Magistrate is directed to send the case to the Special Judge after taking necessary steps as per the decision made by the learned Additional Sessions Judge. The learned Special Judge is directed to dispose of the case within 4 (four) months from the date of receipt of the record from the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka.
